This breaks the header's promise that 'no step rule touches layout before or outside its window', and the before frame no longer matches the original screen.
fix_hint: Where the page CSS defines ::before/::after for a swap or redline selector, make emit refuse or note it. At minimum, document the limit and have check/emit report it. A browser-probe test with an existing ::after clearfix on a redlined element should assert the first frame is unchanged.

title: A later color step on a swapped element brings the old text back under the new text
detail: The swap hides the old text with color:transparent inside the swap animation. Any later step's css animation on the same selector comes later in the animation list and wins for color. Probe: step a swaps .btn, then step b sets .btn {color:#fff}. At the end the element's color is rgb(255,255,255), so the old 'Go' is drawn again under the ::before 'Start free'. check accepts the story, and a palette step after a text swap is a natural ordering.
fix_hint: Have check flag a color change on a swap selector in a step after the swap. Or emit the swap's transparency as the last animation in the list and carry the new ink through later color steps. Add a test for this ordering.

title: check accepts a camera rect beyond the frame width, which renders blank
detail: checkCamera allows x up to 20000. #story-page stays at frame width (1080 or 1920) with overflow:hidden, and cameraCss grows only its height. A rect with x at or beyond the frame width passes check and crops onto clipped, empty space.
fix_hint: In checkCamera, require x + w to be at most the frame width (or widen #story-page to x + w in cameraCss).

title: Swap or redline on img/input is documented as unsupported but check accepts it
detail: The header says swap and redline need a pseudo-element, so not img or input. check still accepts swap {selector:'img'} or redline {selector:'input'} without a problem, and the emitted video just blurs the element or shows no tag.
fix_hint: Make check add a problem (or a note) when a swap or redline selector's last compound starts with img, input or another void element.

title: SIGTERM during the encode orphans the ffmpeg child
detail: onSignal cleans the files and re-raises, but nothing kills the ffmpeg child spawned by exec() (line 224), and the 600 s kill timer dies with node. A SIGTERM sent only to node (from `timeout`, a CI cancel, a supervisor or `kill <pid>`) leaves ffmpeg running under PPID 1. Probe: real Playwright and ffmpeg, 10 s square story, `kill -TERM <node pid>` once the .part.mp4 appeared. Node died with 143, but ffmpeg was still alive with ppid 1. With --keep-frames the orphan encoded the whole sequence and ran 6.5 s after node died. Without it, ffmpeg ran until it hit the deleted frames. For the largest allowed render (120 s, 60 fps, wide) on older or single-core hardware, that is minutes of CPU after the tool reported it had stopped. Ctrl-C in a terminal only works because the TTY signals the whole process group.
fix_hint: Have exec() record the live child, for example in a set the render can reach. In onSignal (and in the finally), call child.kill('SIGKILL') or child.kill(sig) on it before re-raising. Add a real-ffmpeg or stub-child test that checks the child pid is gone after the parent gets SIGTERM.

title: Signal test fires a real SIGINT/SIGTERM event at the whole test process
detail: process.emit(sig, sig) calls every SIGINT/SIGTERM listener in the process, not only the ones story-render added. The suite passes under the default per-file isolation. Under `node --test --experimental-test-isolation=none` (Node 22; `--test-isolation=none` in later Node), the runner's own termination handler fires: the run stops after 'r2 failure paths' subtest 4 with exit 1 and no summary. The test also passes even if render's handler never runs, as long as some other listener happens to clean up.
fix_hint: Compare process.listeners(sig) before and during the render and call only the new listener directly. Do not emit the event process-wide.

title: ffmpeg probe does not check for libx264, so builds without it fail only after the full capture
detail: The header promises ffmpeg is probed before any frame is captured, but the probe only runs `-version`. Distro builds without libx264 pass the probe, for example Fedora's ffmpeg-free and some LGPL static builds. The render then captures every frame (minutes for a 120 s story) and only then fails with 'Unknown encoder libx264' as exit 1. That is not the documented exit 4 for 'ffmpeg missing'.
fix_hint: Also run `<bin> -hide_banner -encoders` in probeFfmpeg and require the libx264 line. Otherwise return exit 4 with a reason naming the missing encoder.

title: Fixed 600 s encode timeout can kill the largest allowed render on older hardware
detail: The cap allows 120 s x 60 fps x 1920x1080 = 7200 frames. Measured with the verb's libx264 settings (crf 18, preset medium) on synthetic 1080p frames: 600 frames took 12.2 s on 4 threads, 18.6 s on 2 threads and 32.4 s on 1 thread. At 7200 frames that is about 150 s, 220 s and 390 s, before any PNG decode cost. An older dual-core or single-core box crosses 600 s and is SIGKILLed after the whole capture is done. No flag raises the limit.
fix_hint: Scale the timeout with the frame count (for example max(600 s, frames x 200 ms)), or add an --encode-timeout flag and document it.

title: Signal path prints a misleading capture error and never names the --keep-frames folder
detail: A SIGTERM during a real capture ends with exit 143, but stderr reads 'kit: frame 23 of 300: the screenshot failed: page.screenshot: Target page, context or browser has been closed'. Playwright's SIGTERM handler closes the browser and the rejected capture is printed before the 100 ms fallback exit, so the operator sees a bogus screenshot bug instead of 'interrupted'. With --keep-frames, the signal path is the one failure path that never says where the frames were kept.
fix_hint: In onSignal, set a flag and write one stderr line such as 'story-render: interrupted by SIGTERM' plus '; frames kept in <dir>' when --keep-frames is set. Have the catch skip printing the capture error once the flag is set.

title: capture hangs forever on an asset response that never finishes; --timeout-ms does not bound it
detail: Every image/font/stylesheet response pushes an async job that awaits r.body() with no timeout, and capture then does `await Promise.all(bodies)`. A body that never completes (an MJPEG/live camera image, a long-poll or stalled chunked asset, here an added after load whose server keeps writing) makes the verb hang with no bound. Probe: 127.0.0.1 server whose page adds an image after load that streams one byte every 500 ms; `capture --url http://127.0.0.1:18923/ --out ... --timeout-ms 5000` was still waiting at 120 s (pw:api trace: response.body started, networkidle wait failed at 5 s, then nothing until the process was killed, then 'the screenshot failed: Target page, context or browser has been closed'). The documented --timeout-ms only covers goto and settle. Applies to the copied helper too (.claude/helpers/kit/page-snapshot.js).
fix_hint: Race each r.body() (or the whole Promise.all(bodies)) against a timer derived from --timeout-ms; a body that misses it is recorded as not captured (e.g. skipped 'response did not finish in time'). Add a real-capture test with a never-ending image response that asserts the capture finishes within the timeout.

title: redirected images are never inlined and are listed as 'the page never loaded it'
detail: Captured bodies are keyed by r.url(), the URL of the final response after redirects, while the copy looks assets up by the element's own URL (img src / currentSrc is the pre-redirect URL). Any image behind a redirect (common for CDNs, /avatar endpoints, same-origin 302s) therefore keeps its remote URL and gets the false skip reason 'the page never loaded it'. Probe on 127.0.0.1: with 302 to /b.png gave inlined:[] and skipped:[{url:'.../redir.png', reason:'the page never loaded it'}], although the browser loaded and displayed it.
fix_hint: When storing a response body, also store it under every URL of its redirect chain (walk r.request().redirectedFrom()), subject to the same private-address check per hop; add a test with a 302'd image.

title: remote mode's forced --no-proxy-server fails behind a mandatory proxy with a misleading error and no option
detail: Remote captures now always launch Chromium with --no-proxy-server (and Node does its own DNS lookups, a failure counting as private). The trade is defensible (through a proxy serverAddr would be the proxy's address and the post-hoc private check would be meaningless), but on a network that only allows egress through HTTP(S)_PROXY (corporate networks, this agent sandbox) a remote capture the user consented to fails as `could not load <url>: net::ERR_...` (exit 1, line 760) with nothing saying the proxy was bypassed on purpose, and every cross-origin asset whose DNS lookup fails is silently aborted and only shown in blocked_origins. The behaviour is stated only in one clause of the header comment; the usage string, the exit-code table and the error text do not mention it, and there is no flag to opt in to a proxy.
fix_hint: Keep the default, but when remote navigation fails and HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY is set, say so in the error (e.g. 'remote mode connects directly, without the configured proxy'); mention it in usage. Optionally add an explicit --proxy-ok flag that uses the proxy and turns off the serverAddr check (documented as weaker).

title: an ambient KIT_EGRESS_ALLOW_EXEC leaks into every packaged test's guard
detail: The harness (test/helpers/packaged.js env()) spreads process.env and overrides KIT_EGRESS_LOG and KIT_EGRESS_ALLOW_DIR but not the new KIT_EGRESS_ALLOW_EXEC. If a developer or CI job has it exported (for example after running this suite by hand), every other packaged test silently allows child processes from those folders, weakening their zero-egress assertions without any sign. With the variable unset, nothing changes for other tests (verified: kit-infra 7/7 pass).
fix_hint: In packaged.js env(), set KIT_EGRESS_ALLOW_EXEC: '' before ...extra so only a test that passes it through extraEnv gets the allowance.

title: exit 4 table omits the old-playwright and remote-guard failures
detail: The exit-code section says 4 means 'playwright or its browser is missing', but capture also returns exit 4 for 'playwright >= 1.48 required' (line 662) and 'the browser cannot apply the remote address guard' (line 714). A caller reading the table cannot tell these apart from a missing install.
fix_hint: List all three causes under exit 4 in the header and usage string.

title: Swap text lands at the left edge of a centred element, not where the old text was
detail: <story-swap> is display:block (line 527) then position:absolute with auto insets, so its static position is the left of the element's content box. text-align is ignored. Probed in Chromium 153 with emitted pages: in a centred h1 the old text spans x 378-702 and the new text x 0-251. In a <button class=btn> (the shape template() swaps) the old text spans x 79-221 and the new text x 12-39. Centred headings and buttons are the normal case for a swap, so the new text visibly jumps sideways on most real stories. No test measures where the new text lands against the old.
fix_hint: Place the swap over the old text's line box: for example, have the parse-time script copy the computed text-align and size the swap to the content box (left:0;right:0 with the element made the containing block only during the swap). Or measure the old text's range rect once and set left/top. Add a Playwright check that compares the old text's range rect with the new text's rect for a text-align:center element and a <button>.

title: Selector camera measures before loading=lazy images load, so the crop misses its target
detail: The header (line 76) says the camera is measured on the load event with 'images loaded'. Lazy images below the 1080px clip of #story-page do not delay load and only start after the camera moves the page. Nothing then re-aims the camera. Probe: a page with a lazy (no width/height) above #target. fit() ran with the image at 0px. The image then loaded at 574px, and #target finished at y=1088, outside the 1080 frame, on every frame. With a rect camera the same images pop in after frame 0. loading=lazy is common in CMS and production pages.
fix_hint: In preparePage, rewrite loading="lazy" to eager (or drop the attribute) so every image counts toward load. Or re-run fit() on each img load event. Correct the header's 'images loaded' claim either way, and add the lazy-image case to the camera Playwright test.

title: Without the script (JS blocked, sandboxed preview) a swapped element goes blank
detail: The swap's fade-out and the hide slot are pure CSS on the element (lines 494-499). The new text exists only once the parse-time <script data-story-marks> inserts <story-swap>. Wherever that script does not run, the old text fades to transparent and stays hidden: an iframe without allow-scripts, a CSP that blocks inline script, an older viewer with JS off, or a tool that strips scripts. The button or heading is left empty from mid-step to the end. Before this round the swap was CSS-only and degraded with it.
fix_hint: Gate the swap's element-side animations on the script having run. For example, the script adds class story-marks to <html>, and the swap slot and hide rules use html.story-play.story-marks. Without the script the old text then simply stays.

title: The page loses the browser's default 8px body margin, so frame 0 is offset from the original
detail: The real <html>/<body> get margin:0 and the page's body content goes into a plain #story-page div, which has no UA body margin. scopeCss carries over only the page's own body rules. So a page that does not reset body margin is drawn 8px up and left of the original, and 16px wider. Its 'before' frame no longer matches the screen being redesigned, and a camera {x,y,w,h} measured on the original page is 8px off. Every fixture writes body{margin:0} or style="margin:0" (test lines 18, 581, 682, 730), which hides this.
fix_hint: Wrap the page body in an inner element that takes the UA body defaults (margin:8px, so margins collapse as in the original) inside the fixed-size #story-page, with the page's scoped body rules on that inner element. Add a frame-0 pixel test on a page without a margin reset.

title: No test still proves a CSS-only story emits no script
detail: The rewrites to match(/<script[^>]*>/gi) === ['<script data-story-marks>'] are as strict as the old !/<script/ for page scripts: any surviving page <script> adds an entry. But each fixture now swaps or redlines, so the header's rule that the script is emitted only when a step swaps or redlines or the camera follows a selector is never tested in its negative case. A regression that always emits the marks or camera script would pass.
fix_hint: Add an emit of a story with css-only steps and no selector camera, and assert html.match(/<script/gi) is null.

title: fonts.ready wait has no bound: a stalled late font hangs capture forever
detail: After the settle, capture runs page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready) with no timeout and nothing tied to the --timeout-ms deadline. If a web font is requested after the load event (text that gets a font-family once it renders, which is common in SPAs, or content revealed later) and its body stalls, which is normal on a degraded network, fonts.ready never resolves and the verb hangs. Probe: a 127.0.0.1 page whose h1 switches to an @font-face family 20 ms after load, with the font sending headers plus 10 bytes and then stalling. `capture --timeout-ms 3000` sat in this evaluate until an outside `timeout 120` killed it. Instrumented copy: 'fonts start' at +3.8 s, the evaluate returned only when the browser was torn down 56 s later. The header (lines 28-31) says --timeout-ms bounds the load, the settle and every asset body wait together. The other post-load waits also ignore the deadline: settle is Math.min(timeout, 10000) and then Math.min(timeout, 5000) for --full-page, not the time left, and the screenshot has a fixed 15000 ms. So even a run that does not hang can take about timeout + 30 s.
fix_hint: Take every post-goto wait from the deadline that remains: race fonts.ready against a timer inside the evaluate (for example Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))])) and set networkIdle-style flags when it runs out. Pass deadline - Date.now() (with a small floor) to both settle calls and to the screenshot timeout. Add a test with a stalled post-load font that must finish within --timeout-ms plus a margin.

title: Stalled asset in the initial markup fails the whole capture (exit 1, nothing written)
detail: page.goto uses waitUntil:'load', and the load event waits for every image, stylesheet and font the document requested before load. One asset in the original HTML whose body stalls (a slow CDN on a degraded network, a chunked image that never ends) makes goto throw 'Timeout exceeded', and the verb exits 1 with 'could not load' and writes no files. Probe: on 127.0.0.1, with stall.png sending 4 bytes and then nothing; `capture --timeout-ms 3000` gave exit 1 and no out dir. The header (lines 28-31) promises that a body still unfinished when the budget is spent, 'a streaming or stalled image, say', is dropped and listed in skipped, and that the files are still written with exit 0. The r2 test covers only an image added after load (test line 855), so the common case goes untested.
fix_hint: Navigate with waitUntil:'domcontentloaded' (or catch a goto TimeoutError once a response has been committed) and then wait for 'load' with the time left, setting a load/network_idle flag instead of failing. The existing body-deadline path then marks the stalled asset BODY_LATE. Add a real-capture test with a stalled in the initial markup.

title: /mt slop gate: per-file measure lets the last clean file hide an earlier dirty one
detail: The 4.3c slop audit says to scan every changed screen file on each loop pass, and after each scan to record `record measure key=slop_<s> value=true` on exit 0 or `value=false` on exit 2. All files of the stream write to the same key, and gate.js resolveSource (measure:) takes the LAST row for the key. Your own reach test checks this: met([false, true]) === true. So a stream with two screens, where a.html still has slop (false) and b.html scanned after it is clean (true), meets `slop_<s>`, and the blocking gate passes with unresolved signs. That is a normal input: most UI streams change more than one file. Installed copy: .claude/commands/.shortcuts/w-marathon.md:421.
fix_hint: Record one measure per pass: value=true only when every changed screen file's scan exited 0, otherwise value=false. One way is to scan all files in one block and record from the combined status. Add a reach test with one dirty and one clean file.

title: /pt blocking do-not check is not enforced for a new screen (template-test always exits 0)
detail: The CHECKPOINT 6 Review step is BLOCKING ('failures stop the review'). For a new screen with no before version it says to run `template-test --name "$PRODUCT_NAME" --file "$AFTER"` instead, but no block runs that command and nothing says to read `pass`. template-test has no --strict: it exits 0 even with pass:false. I probed it: a page without the product name, made only of generic sentences, gave pass:false and rc=0, and adding --strict gave rc=1 (unexpected argument). The text after the step reads 'Exit 0: no do-not violation and the template test passes; go on', so on this path a failed template test is read as a pass. New landing pages and new dashboards are a common case. Installed copy: .claude/commands/.shortcuts/w-plan-tdd-swarm.md:675.
fix_hint: Add a block for the new-screen path and state that `pass: false` from template-test stops the review exactly like exit 2. Or have the no-before path go through a command that exits 2 on a false pass. Add a reach test for it.

title: /mt image gate stops the unattended loop to wait on AskUserQuestion, against 'Ask once'
detail: The 4.3c image gate says to 'put it to the user exactly as printed (AskUserQuestion) and wait for the answer' in the middle of the loop. /w-marathon's Rules say 'Ask once. After the kickoff is approved, the only questions left are the waitingOnHuman lines', and the Interview says Claude 'never stops to wait'. The spec row says 'declined means an empty slot, not a stalled loop', but an unanswered request (pending) stalls the loop for as long as the owner is away. A days-long run then sits idle on one image prompt. The kit-missing fallback has the same problem: it asks in plain words and waits. Installed copy: .claude/commands/.shortcuts/w-marathon.md:340.
fix_hint: In /mt, while the request is pending: put the slot in place, list the request as a waitingOnHuman / checklist.md line (the report already lists pending requests) and carry on. Or collect the image approvals in the Interview batch. Never block the loop on an AskUserQuestion.

title: /mt slop finish line is added even without the kit, so a UI stream can never meet its gate
detail: The Interview adds the `slop_<s>` line (source measure:slop_<s>) for every UI, landing page or dashboard stream, whether or not the kit is installed. Only the 4.3c slop audit, which is kit-only, ever records that measure. In a project without .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js the step 'is skipped like every kit step', the measure is never written, gate.js returns NOT_FOUND, and the stream's gate stays unmet forever. That breaks the promise that 'the kit is advisory and never blocks a workflow that worked before', and it hits every UI stream, not only the reference-design ones the fidelity line covers.
fix_hint: Add the slop_<s> line only when .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js exists, the same condition as the step that records it. Or record value=true with a 'kit not installed' note when the audit is skipped.

title: Triage scan redirect writes a file named after the placeholder when AUDIT is unfilled
detail: In both /pt (CHECKPOINT 1) and /mt (Kickoff), the block warns when AUDIT still holds the placeholder but runs anyway. `slop-audit scan ... > "$AUDIT"` then creates a stray file named '<a new file path for the audit JSON>' in the project root, and the next grade line reads it. Installed copy: w-plan-tdd-swarm.md:213.
fix_hint: Skip the redirect when the placeholder check fires, for example `case "$AUDIT" in '<'*) (exit 1);; *) node ... > "$AUDIT";; esac`.

title: Without the kit, the image check always exits 2, which conflicts with 'ask, then call on a yes'
detail: With no kit, the step says to ask the yes/no in plain words and 'call no image tool before a yes', so a yes should allow the call. But the check block's fallback always exits 2, and the text right after it says '**Exit 2 stops: do not call the image tool.**' A model that follows the exit code never generates an image even after the user says yes, and a workflow that generated images before is blocked.
fix_hint: After the check block, add one sentence for the no-kit case: the exit 2 comes from the missing kit, and the user's plain-words yes is what allows the call.

title: on* handler stripping is bypassed by a '/' separator or a '<' in an unquoted value, and the handlers run in the render
detail: The header (line 52) and preparePage (line 461) promise the emitted page has its on* handlers removed. HANDLER only matches an attribute that follows whitespace (\s+on...), and TAG (line 133) fails to match a tag whose unquoted value holds '<'. Probe: a --page body with ``, `` and `` comes out of `story-plan emit` unchanged. Loaded in Chromium (Playwright, file:// URL as story-render loads it), all three ran: requests to example.com/x and example.com/y and an alert('2') dialog. So page script runs in a page the docs call script-free. That makes the frames nondeterministic, can reach localhost (story-render allows it), and has open egress when the page is opened by hand through story-render play. I graded this medium, not high: the input is the author's own page, and story-render blocks hosts that are not local.
fix_hint: Match a handler after whitespace or '/' (e.g. (?:\s|/)+on[a-z]+ ...), and when TAG cannot parse a tag (an unquoted value holds '<' or a stray quote), drop any on[a-z]+= in that tag text with a fallback pass. Add these three probes to the strip test.

title: A <meta http-equiv=refresh> or <base href> in the body is kept and moves the render off the story page
detail: scanPage drops head content but keeps any meta or base element inside , and browsers honour both there. Probe: a body with `` is emitted as it is. In Chromium the page requested http://example.com/base/rel.png (every relative asset now points at a remote host) and then navigated away to http://example.com/r, so the render ended on chrome-error://chromewebdata/ instead of the story. preparePage says the page is 'made safe to play', but here the page leaves for a remote host and the captured frames are not the story.
fix_hint: In scanPage, drop base tags, and meta tags with http-equiv (at least refresh), wherever they appear, and count them in stripped. Add a test for a body-level meta refresh and base.

title: Comment scanning differs from the HTML parser: script-made <!--> comments let on* handlers through to the copy
detail: scanHtml ends a comment at the next literal '-->' (indexOf from lt+4). The HTML parser also ends a comment at '', '' and '--!>'. outerHTML writes comment data unchanged, so a page script that runs document.body.appendChild(document.createComment('>')) is serialized as '-->'. scanHtml reads all of that as one comment and never looks at the img, so the onerror attribute stays in page.html. A browser reads '' as an empty comment and then parses a real . I probed it with a file:// page: the onerror in the saved page.html ran when the copy was opened (window.__y was set). That breaks the stated promise 'Nothing runs when the copy is opened', and any page captured with --allow-remote can trigger it.
fix_hint: Make the comment branch follow the parser's end rules: '<!-->' and '<!--->' end at once, otherwise stop at the first '-->' or '--!>'. Better still, have snapshotDom drop or neutralize comment nodes in the clone, for example by replacing '-' and '>' in their data, so a comment can never hide markup.

title: noscript raw text plus the keep-the-rest-verbatim fallback leaves <script> in the copy
detail: With scripting on, Chromium serializes
fix_hint: Add noscript to RAW_TEXT, the same way the serializer treats it. Make scanHtml fail closed: when a comment or tag is unterminated, drop the remainder or throw, never copy it verbatim. Add a test that asserts no '<script' and no ' on*=' survive these inputs.

title: WebRTC (STUN/TURN) skips every network guard and reaches private hosts in remote mode
detail: The request route, the WebSocket route and the CDP Fetch guard only see HTTP and WebSocket traffic. RTCPeerConnection ICE traffic goes past all three. In remote mode the browser is launched with only --no-proxy-server, so a page's script can make it open TCP connections (TURN ?transport=tcp) and send UDP (STUN) to any address. I probed a remote-mode page at http://127.0.0.2 that created an RTCPeerConnection with turn:127.0.0.3:18094?transport=tcp and stun:127.0.0.3:18095. The listener on 127.0.0.3 logged 'TCP connect' and two UDP packets during the capture, and blocked_origins did not list them. The doc's claim that no request may reach a loopback, private or link-local host does not hold, and a page can use this to probe ports on the internal network or 169.254.169.254. In local mode the same path reaches any IP literal, so the claim that everything else is blocked at the browser fails there as well.
fix_hint: Turn WebRTC off in the capture browser: add a ctx.addInitScript that deletes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection and RTCDataChannel (it runs in every frame, about:blank included), and/or launch with --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp together with a dead proxy for WebRTC. Add a test with a local TURN/STUN listener on 127.0.0.x that asserts no connection reaches it.

title: page.evaluate(snapshotDom) has no deadline, so a busy page hangs the capture past --timeout-ms + 6 s
detail: This round says the deadline covers every wait, but the DOM pass after the screenshot (line 900) is awaited with no bound. The per-pending-stylesheet privateUrl DNS checks at line 911 also have no bound. When the page's main thread is busy after the screenshot, evaluate never returns. I probed it with a file:// page that runs setTimeout(() => { for(;;); }, 520..540 ms) and --timeout-ms 2000: the capture was still running when I killed it at 30 s, against a stated limit of 8 s. A hostile or very heavy remote page can therefore hang the verb and the agent workflow that calls it with no end, which contradicts the documented 'A capture ends within --timeout-ms plus 6 s'.
fix_hint: Wrap the snapshotDom evaluate in bounded(..., Math.max(SCREENSHOT_FLOOR_MS, left()), null) and throw exit 1 ('the page did not answer in time') on null. Bound the hostVerdict lookups the same way, treating a timeout as private. Add a test with a page that busy-loops after the screenshot.

title: Reduced motion still plays the swap's blur-out and fade on the swapped element
detail: Under prefers-reduced-motion a swap's only reduced rule is for the inserted <story-swap> (opacity 1, animation none). The swapped element keeps its story-wN animation from the shared stack (no reduced rule sets animation:none on swap.selector unless that selector also has a css step or redline). Probe: story with a swap on .btn only, Chromium reducedMotion 'reduce', at t=2300ms (mid-tween) .btn has filter blur(8px) and opacity 0, and the new text, a child of it, blurs and fades with it. That contradicts the header line 104 claim 'Under prefers-reduced-motion the final state is shown', and it puts the blur motion back in front of viewers who asked for less motion. The test named 'swap uses blur-out and blur-in, with reduced-motion final state' (test line 313) checks only the keyframe text, and the browser reduced-motion test (line 791) uses a selector that also has a css step, whose reduced animation:none hides the bug.
fix_hint: In the swap branch, push `html.story-play :is(${w.selector}){animation:none !important}` (or animation-name:none) into `reduced`; the stack's reduced rule already holds the old text transparent. Add a browser assertion with reducedMotion 'reduce' on a swap-only selector: filter none and opacity 1 at mid-tween.

title: The page's lang and dir are dropped: an RTL page renders LTR and every page is labelled lang="en"
detail: scanPage drops the <html> tag with all its attributes (lines 369/373), preparePage keeps only class and style from <body> (line 551), and emit hard-codes <html lang="en">. Probe: <html lang="ar" dir="rtl"> with an Arabic h1 gives computed direction 'ltr' and documentElement.lang 'en' in the emitted page. An Arabic or Hebrew page comes out mirrored wrong, so frame 0 no longer matches the original; :lang() rules, CJK glyph choice and hyphenation change too, and assistive tech reading the page gets the wrong language.
fix_hint: Carry lang and dir from the original <html> (and dir/lang from <body>) onto the emitted <html> (or #story-page/#story-body), escaped, falling back to lang="en" only when the page has none; add a test with dir="rtl".

title: on* handlers survive after a '--!>' comment end and inside svg <title>/<textarea>
detail: The header promises on* handlers removed. Three cases still produce live handlers in the emitted page (Chromium probe, each onerror ran): (1) ` -->`: a browser ends the comment at '--!>', but scanPage and cleanTags (line 486) look only for '-->', so the img is treated as comment text and kept as is; (2) `` and (3) ``: RAWTEXT/RCDATA (line 316) treat title and textarea as raw text everywhere, but inside svg (foreign content) they are not, so the markup inside is parsed and its handler runs. The same reading also skips a
fix_hint: End comments at the first of '-->', '--!>' (and '<!-->'/'<!--->') in both scanners; skip title/textarea as raw text only outside <svg>/<math> (track a foreign-content depth), or drop the raw-text skip and over-strip instead. Add each of the three cases to the stripping tests.

title: Swap text defaults to #111 whatever the element's own text colour
detail: With no swap.ink, the new text is #111 even when the element's text is light. The template swaps .btn with no ink. Probe: a button with white text on #1d4ed8 shows the new label in #111 at about 2.8:1 contrast, below the 4.5:1 AA level, and the original label was 6.7:1. The swap-ink note fires only when a step changes color on the swap selector, so a check gives no warning here. The browser test at test line 791 asserts ink rgb(17,17,17) on a final background of rgb(0,0,0), which is unreadable text written into a passing test.
fix_hint: When ink is not given, have the marks script copy the element's computed color at t=0 (inside z(place)) onto the <story-swap>. Or add a check note that names the default ink whenever a swap has no ink.

title: /mt fix rounds never re-run the blocking slop audit, so a stale slop_<s>=true can meet the gate
detail: The slop audit lives in 4.3c, which runs on each loop pass after 4.3b and before 4.4. But 4.7 Fix round ends with 'Back to 4.4' (w-marathon.md:521), skipping 4.3/4.3b/4.3c. A fixer that edits a screen file (for example rewrites copy for a review finding) is never scanned, and 4.8 then reads the latest slop_<s> measure, which is the true recorded on the pass before the fix. The finish line looks enforced but is not on this path. The fidelity step solved the same problem with an explicit sentence ('a fix round (4.7 -> 4.4) on such a stream scores fidelity again before 4.4', line 5311); the slop step has no such sentence, and no reach test covers a fix round.
fix_hint: Add to the slop audit paragraph (and the 4.7 text): 'a fix round (4.7 -> 4.4) on a UI stream runs this block again over the changed screen files before 4.4', and add a reach-test assertion that the sentence is there.

title: /pt Build image gate still asks and waits mid-loop when /mt builds through /pt
detail: /mt 4.3 tells the loop to 'build through /pt ... skip straight to its Plan gate', which runs /pt's CHECKPOINT 5 Build. The new /pt image-gate step says 'put it to the user exactly as printed (AskUserQuestion) and wait for the answer' (w-plan-tdd-swarm.md:495), and nothing in /pt says what to do when it runs inside an unattended /w-marathon loop. The r1 fix made /mt 4.3c queue the request and never ask mid-loop, but a /mt stream that generates an image through /pt's Build step hits the /pt wording and stalls on the question. That breaks the /mt row's 'declined means an empty slot, not a stalled loop'.
fix_hint: In the /pt image-gate step add one sentence: when /pt runs as the build of a /w-marathon stream, do not ask: queue the request as /w-marathon 4.3c says (place the slot, add the checklist.md line) and go on.

title: Every power is recorded with reach: [], so delivered.md cannot name the reach test
detail: All 10 powers were recorded with --verb only. The workflow targets still count as wired (the verb runs in the step), but `delivered` writes 'the test that proves it' from the reach rows, and `wired` reports test: null for every target. test/bbs-unslop-reach.test.js exists and passes, but the owner's hand-over note will not point to it.
fix_hint: Re-run `cli.js integrate --power <name> --verb <verb> --reach workflow:<file>@<heading>=test/bbs-unslop-reach.test.js::node --test test/bbs-unslop-reach.test.js` for each wired target (use --force if needed).

title: A swap text wider than its element spills out of it, and the template's own example does so on a small button
detail: The <story-swap> is out of flow, white-space:nowrap and width:max-content, centred over the old text, and the element keeps its size. So new text wider than the element's box runs past its edges. I rendered the template story over a page whose .btn is a pill button with the label "Go" (about 42px wide, align-self:flex-start). At t=4500 the 55px-wide "Start free" hangs about 7px past each side of the button. Its white ink is invisible on the light card there, so the label reads "tart fre". The header describes the swap as "one line as wide as the new text" moved over the old text, but its 'Limits of the inserted swap child' list never says that a longer label overflows the element. The template, which is the example authors copy, swaps a short CTA to a longer one without saying so. It is advisory, the page is the author's own and the author sees it in a preview, so this is low.
fix_hint: Add one line to the swap limits in the header: the element keeps its size, so new text wider than it overflows; widen it with a padding step first. Optionally put a note in the template's step (or make its swap text no longer than a typical short label).

title: Header says pill-radius fires at 999px and up; check fires at 500px
detail: The rules table says 'pill-radius  a pill radius (999px and up) cannot tween', but check() flags any plain radius >= 500 (line 260: Number(m[1]) >= 500). So an author who reads the header and writes border-radius 600px gets an unexpected pill-radius problem, and ok becomes false.
fix_hint: Change the header to '(500px and up)', or make the code threshold match the documented 999.
